reason: Supported. The delivered entry scripts/recap_fragments.py wraps the inspected upstream RDKit module rdkit/Chem/Recap.py at commit 237a1d9027c800784afed8788540f38a3aa595f8. The script imports rdkit.Chem.Recap, parses the SMILES with Chem.MolFromSmiles, calls Recap.RecapDecompose(mol), then returns sorted(root.GetLeaves().keys()); the quoted upstream function signature establishes that exact API. The adapter adds blank/zero-atom guards, JSON serialization and error labels, but does not reimplement chemistry. Run under Python 3 in an RDKit-enabled container. From the skill directory, the one positional argument is a single quoted SMILES string; an absolute script path can be used from another working directory. The script writes no files, prints one JSON object to stdout, exits 0 for successful decomposition (including empty fragment lists) and 2 for empty_input, invalid_smiles, empty_molecule, or argparse errors. RDKit compiled dependencies must be available; no external data or model weights are required.
